steps.minor: {a} minor uses the same white keys as {c} major, but its home note is {a}, and it sounds darker. These are its first five notes.
steps.leadingNote: Minor pieces often raise the seventh note, {g}, to {gSharp}: a half step below {a}, it leans back home. {a} minor has no key signature, so the sharp is written in the music each time.
steps.findMinor: Find the five notes, and {gSharp} just below them.
steps.minorTune: A short tune in {a} minor. The thumb plays {gSharp}; finger 2 is on {a}.
steps.greensleeves: “Greensleeves”, an English tune more than 400 years old, in {a} minor. Watch for the sharps: {gSharp}, and {fSharp} on the way back up.
steps.greensleevesBoth: Now with the left hand: one long note in each bar.
